notes.src/civilization/simulation.js: Re-baselined twice. (1) v13 geography-driven district names. (2) Sea lanes are now straightened after the flood fill finds them, so route.path holds the corners a vessel would turn at instead of a N/S/E/W staircase. Only that derived array changes: the BFS distance used to rank trade partners is untouched, and physicalFingerprint dfd91476, settlementFingerprint 77c3b21f and politicalFingerprint (which hashes province ownership alone) are all unchanged. Asserted in tests/onemap.test.mjs and tests/continuous.test.mjs.
notes.src/world/geography.js: Re-baselined for legendary places. nameLegends() runs after every physical pass has finished and writes only w.legends / w.legendStats; it reads the finished fields and moves nothing. physicalFingerprint is dfd91476 before and after the change, asserted in tests/onemap.test.mjs, so the geography itself is byte-identical.
notes.src/render/world-renderer.js: Re-baselined for two deliberate rendering changes. (a) Map clarity: supersampled backing store in resize(), Geometry.smoothTri() for per-vertex terrain normals and colours, buildLegends() markers. (b) Political layers: realms and diplomacy no longer paint a country's territory at all. Every border already carries a cased frontier line, and that is the whole of the country on this map; only the realm you have selected takes a faint wash, so the selection is answerable. Faiths, peoples, wealth and magic keep their full colour, where the colour is the measurement. Terrain vertex positions are untouched: the surface is locked by AtlasSpace.surface parity and the shared-edge check in tests/continuous.test.mjs, and the political palette by the coverage assertion in tests/onemap.test.mjs. The v12 shader and layer-visibility normalisations are folded into this baseline.
